correctness.rationale: For n>=5, dihedral averaging preserves feasibility and does not increase the norm. A c>0 first-mode Loewner comparison and r-independent positive Rayleigh vector yield the claimed universal bound. The proposed weights exactly realize the Rayleigh equality; elementary n=5,6 and uniform n>=7 inequalities ensure 0<r<1/2 and feasibility; comparison to B_- plus 1-p controls every negative Fourier mode; the radial characteristic quadratic controls both remaining modes. Unique invariant equality follows from strict positive coordinates and eigenvector matching. Exact-symbolic checks and dense reproductions on the packaged verify.py supported the proof, without treating finite tests as infinite proofs.

value.rationale: The helm graph is a canonical wheel-plus-leaves family, and the third transition orbit produces a genuinely nonlinear exact optimum rather than the known wheel formula. The result gives an all-size SLEM and optimizer, proves precise zero-holding saturation and uniqueness within invariant weights, and establishes a quantitative large-size spectral-gap advantage over maximum-degree weighting. This is an exact network-design classification with a clear application to fast uniform-stationary mixing.
